37 In the circuits shown, the cell has negligible internal resistance.
Which diagram shows a potential divider circuit that can vary the potential difference (p.d.) across
the lamp?
A
B
C
D

hints: Look at what the lamp is connected across in each circuit - directly across the cell terminals or across only part of the variable resistor.
Recall a variable potential divider needs the cell across the whole resistance track and the output taken between the sliding contact and one fixed end.
Imagine moving the slider to the top and then to the bottom of the track and ask in which circuit the lamp p.d. would change from full e.m.f. to zero.
walkthrough: Note the cell has negligible internal resistance, so the terminal p.d. equals the e.m.f. and the task is to find where the lamp samples a variable fraction of it.
A potential divider requires $V_{out} = V_{in} \times R_2/(R_1 + R_2)$, with the supply across $R_1 + R_2$ and the load across only $R_2$ where the slider splits the track.
In the correct circuit the top and bottom of the resistor track connect to the cell, and one side of the lamp connects to the slider while the other connects to the bottom wire.

Moving the slider up increases the resistance $R_2$ below the contact that is in parallel with the lamp, so the share of the e.m.f. across the lamp increases toward maximum, and moving it down decreases it toward zero.
The other circuits fail this test because the lamp is wired directly across the cell or the variable resistor is only in series or in parallel without a sliding tap.
Only the slider potentiometer connection gives a continuously variable p.d. across the lamp. This is option C

A.explanation: The lamp is connected directly across the cell, so its p.d. equals the e.m.f. and changing the parallel variable resistor does not divide the voltage.

B.explanation: The variable resistor is in series with the lamp and acts as a rheostat, so it varies current but does not form a divider with the lamp tapped across part of a track.

C.explanation: The cell is across the full resistor track and the lamp is connected between the sliding contact and the bottom, so moving the slider varies the fraction of the e.m.f. across the lamp from zero to maximum.

D.explanation: The slider is shorted to the top of the track and the lamp is across the cell, so the lamp always sees full e.m.f. and no division occurs.
